x: Both statements are true: the Brahmo Samaj (1828) was the earliest modern reform movement, and Veeresalingam, inspired by Rammohan Roy, spread it in Andhra. The APPSC key links them as assertion and explanation.
dispute: APPSC key: A and R true, R explains A. Strictly R (Brahmo Samaj in Andhra) does not explain why the Samaj was the earliest reform movement, so 'R is not the correct explanation' is the stricter answer.
source: APPSC key; NextGen Modern India (Veeresalingam & Brahmo Samaj)

x: The printed key: an atrocity under the PoA Act cannot be defended as the exercise of the right of private defence. The Act also bars anticipatory bail (Sec. 18) and requires the accused to be a non-SC/ST.
dispute: Printed key: private defence. Strictly the IPC general exceptions, private defence included, still apply to PoA offences, so 'None of the above' is arguable (PoA Act 1989 original text (web: hrw.org/legacy/reports/1999/india/India994-16.h).
